severity: operational; no cap breach, no result corruption, no decision-store impact
what_happened: the operating assistant launched a second auto-resume supervisor while the first was still alive; the first had not exited at worklist export because that pass ALSO halted on a provider transient (export happens on halted passes too), and the operator misread the monitor's export event as clean termination. Two driver processes then appended concurrently to the hash-chained usage ledger and call cache for roughly 40 minutes
detection: the surviving first supervisor's next driver invocation refused at load: 'usage ledger chain discontinuity at sequence 1671'; a stale monitor surfaced the refusal
root_cause: no single-instance enforcement anywhere in the live path; the supervisor's exit contract conflates 'worklist exported cleanly' (rc 0) with 'halted with a partial export' (rc nonzero, keeps running); the operator relaunched without verifying process death
remediation: all canary processes killed before any further writes

usage ledger and call cache migrated explicitly: originals preserved byte-for-byte as *.incident1-2026-07-28; fresh ledger genesis with the conservative spend carried forward via the ledger binding (carried_forward_actual/uncertain), so the cap counts every cent of the incident window; cache rebuilt deterministically from the preserved rows through a fresh chain (no provider calls, no spend)
results and decision store untouched (validated clean)

code: run_live now takes an exclusive non-blocking flock on <archive>/canary.lock for its whole duration and refuses if held; the supervisor takes <archive>/supervisor.lock the same way; both refusals are loud
migration runs only via an explicit CLI flag that requires this record to exist on disk
scientific_impact: none identified: no cell executed twice, no result row duplicated or lost, reviewer decisions single-writer throughout; the incident window affected only accounting-integrity metadata, which is why the strict chains caught it
adjudication: flagged for the adjudicator alongside the other operational records of this epoch
note: Append-only. Grants no authority and changes no cap.
